story-context.summary: Build a Grid Layout system as an alternative to Object Layout, allowing users to arrange component objects (label, input, validation, etc.) in a flexible CSS Grid structure with configurable rows, columns, spacing, and cell merging capabilities.
story-context.problem-statement: The current Object Layout system has constraints for complex form layouts. Component Framework issues are blocking UAT testing for Stories 3.8 and 3.9. Grid Layout provides a more robust layout system with precise positioning control.

key-features.feature: Grid Layout Modal - Configure rows, columns, gaps via visual editor
Object Assignment - Drag-and-drop objects onto grid cells
Cell Merging - Combine cells for objects spanning multiple cells
Individual Spacing - Per-row and per-column gap customization
Global Defaults - Form-wide defaults with component overrides

reference-documents.document: Comprehensive Grid Layout specification with schema, mockups, and implementation notes
Component Framework reference for object structure and layout patterns
Story 3.10 definition with requirements and acceptance criteria

key-types.type: Main configuration interface for grid layout (rows, columns, gaps, assignments)
Extended with defaultGridLayout? for form-wide defaults

key-files.file: Grid layout helper functions (CSS generation, cell assignment, merging)
Render grid layout when gridLayout is configured

done-criteria.criterion: Grid Layout modal opens and saves configuration correctly
Objects can be assigned to grid cells via drag-and-drop
Grid renders correctly on canvas and in runtime preview
Component overrides work independently of global defaults
Grid Layout does NOT break existing Object Layout functionality

out-of-scope.item: Auto-migration from Object Layout to Grid Layout

downstream.dependency: Public Form Renderer - benefits from improved layout
Builder Persistence - Grid Layout saved in FormVersion

risks.risk: New layout system must not break existing Object Layout functionality
CSS Grid browser compatibility (all modern browsers support it)
